paragraphs: AWS's managed private Git repositories: repositories, pull requests, triggers and events for pipelines, IAM access, encryption, and when to use a third-party Git provider through CodeConnections instead.

AWS CodeCommit is a managed, secure source control service that hosts private Git repositories. It supports standard Git, so existing Git tools work, and it adds pull requests with reviews, notifications, and integration with IAM and other AWS services. There are no servers to manage, and repositories are encrypted at rest and in transit.

Choose CodeCommit when a question asks for private Git repositories hosted in AWS, with access controlled by IAM, as the source for a release pipeline (MLA-C02 task 3.3.2). If the code already lives on GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket, connect it with AWS CodeConnections instead of moving it.

IAM policies control access; data is encrypted at rest with KMS (an AWS managed key or a customer managed keyCustomer managed keyA KMS key that you create, own, and manage: you control its key policy, rotation, and deletion. AWS managed keys, in contrast, are created and managed for you by an AWS service.Glossary entryClose) and in transit; CloudTrail records APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose calls; approval rules enforce code review.
CodeCommit stores repositories redundantly as a managed service. Git itself is distributed, so every clone holds the history.
Git works best for source code: version large, frequently changing files in Amazon S3 instead, and delete branches and tags you no longer need.
You pay per active user per month above the free allowance, with additional charges for storage and Git requests above the included amounts.
EventBridge events and SNS notifications report pushes, pull requests, and comments; CloudTrail logs access.
